title: Returned Payment History and the Form of the Late Charge on a Reinstated Schedule
content:
How the late charge on a deduction schedule that a returned remittance reinstated is worked out, under the Paystride Earned Wage Access Program Agreement, follows the employer's returned payments. The returns counted are the remittance returns booked on the agreement and the funding returns booked on the employer's Paystride Payroll Card Program, on entry dates from which fewer than 12 whole months have passed to today, a whole month from an entry date being reached on the same day of the month as that entry date, or on the first day of the next month where that month has no such day:

| Returns counted, both kinds together | Late charge |
|---|---|
| 3 or more | the tier's minimum late charge plus the rate applied to the whole returned amount, rounded half up to the cent |
| exactly 2 | the tier's minimum late charge plus the percentage charge |
| fewer than 2 | the greater of the tier's minimum late charge and the percentage charge |

The whole returned amount is the amount of the remittance return that reinstated the schedule; the percentage charge is the rate applied to the schedule's open amount, rounded half up to the cent.

## Illustration (hypothetical: minimum 50.00, rate 1.25 percent, return of 12600.00, schedule now open by 3600.00)

- Two remittance returns and one Payroll Card funding return in the window: 50.00 plus 157.50, a late charge of 207.50.
- One remittance return and one Payroll Card funding return: 50.00 plus 45.00, that is 95.00.
- Only the one remittance return: the greater of 50.00 and 45.00, that is 50.00.
